author: Gregory Thaumaturgus
occasion: Tatian has asked Gregory to send him a discourse and disputation on the soul using effective arguments or demonstrations, and that in this matter he use no testimonies of Scripture. Tatian wants the work to convince those who think otherwise and refuse to believe the divine Scriptures, who use their skill in disputation to circumvent and deceive people unaccustomed to such debate.
argument: Gregory agrees to write on the soul using only human reasoning and common notions, not Scripture, at Tatian's request. He will follow the customary order of inquiry used by those who treat such subjects. He will first propose the criterion by which the soul can be grasped according to nature, then show by what arguments its existence is demonstrated, whether it is substance or accident, body or incorporeal, simple or composite, mortal or immortal, and finally whether it partakes of reason or not. For proofs he will use common notions by which assent is usually obtained for things that are handled by the hands, choosing only the reasonings most effective for demonstrating each point.

outline.move: Gregory addresses Tatian, explains why he has undertaken to write on the soul using only rational arguments without Scripture, and lays out the order of questions he will investigate.

cast.name: Tatian
cast.who: The addressee, a friend of Gregory already instructed in divine Scriptures and traditions, who requested this work.

cast.name: Gregory Thaumaturgus
cast.who: The author, who was persuaded by these reasons not to shun the treatise out of ignorance, but trusting in Tatian's goodwill toward him, promptly complied with Tatian's request and will.

key_terms.sense: The soul, the subject of the entire inquiry.
Effective proofs or arguments, contrasted with scriptural testimonies.
Testimonies or citations from the divine Scriptures, which Gregory is asked not to use.
Common notions or generally accepted conceptions by which assent is given to evident things.
Substance, as opposed to accident, one of the questions to be investigated about the soul.
Partaking of reason, i.e., rational, as opposed to lacking reason.
The criterion or standard by which the soul can be grasped according to nature.

scripture: Gregory explicitly says he will not use scriptural testimonies in this work, so no scriptural naming conventions are employed here.
uncertain: Whether the work as transmitted is complete or only a preface to a longer treatise.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Tatian wants the work to convince those who think otherwise and refuse to believe the divine Scriptures, who use their skill in disputation to circumvent and deceive people unaccustomed to such debate.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: non ut tibi ipse satisfacias, quippe qui iam ita sis instructus, ut Divinis et Scripturis, et traditionibus atque constitutionibus adhaereas, neque ullis humanis rationibus de sententia dimoveri te sinas; sed ad eos convincendos qui aliter sentiunt, et Scripturis divinis fidem habere nolunt; quadam autem differendi facultate homines disputationi eiusmodi haud assuetos circumvenire ac fallere nituntur
_unresolved_facts.fix: Tatian himself is already so instructed that he adheres to divine Scriptures and traditions and cannot be moved by human reasonings; rather, the work is to convince those others who think otherwise, refuse to believe divine Scriptures, and try to circumvent and deceive people unaccustomed to such debate by their skill in disputation.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The addressee, a friend of Gregory already instructed in divine Scriptures and traditions, who requested this work.
_unresolved_facts.fix: The addressee, a friend of Gregory already instructed in divine Scriptures, traditions, and constitutions (constitutionibus), who requested this work.

_unresolved_facts.claim: For proofs he will use common notions by which assent is usually obtained for things that are handled by the hands
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: notionibus illis utemur communibus, per quas rebus quae manibus tractantur, assensus comparari solet
_unresolved_facts.fix: For proofs he will use common notions, through which assent is usually obtained for things that are handled by the hands

_unresolved_facts.claim: choosing only the reasonings most effective for demonstrating each point
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: iis duntaxat nunc ratiocinationibus utemur, quae ad demonstranda illa, quorum fit investigatio, potissimum valent
_unresolved_facts.fix: using only those reasonings which are most powerful for demonstrating the things under investigation
